title: Presence from_cbor still skips mutation-safe CBOR checks
description:
File: rust/lichen-client/src/presence.rs (Presence::from_cbor, PresenceCache::from_cbor, PresenceClient get/put/get_cache)

4qlx added Cursor leftover rejection. from_cbor still does ciborium serde into the struct with no duplicate-key, tag, or size/depth scan.

Python PUT /presence uses _decode_single_cbor (python/src/lichen/coap/resources/cbor_validation.py): reject trailing items, duplicate map keys, CBOR tags, payloads > 4096 bytes, depth > 16, maps > 64, arrays > 256. Sibling lichen-client ConfigUpdate already applies those mutation limits. serde last-wins on duplicate keys (status twice can flip available vs emergency). Tags may decode. PresenceClient feeds untrusted GET /presence and GET /presence/cache payloads through these decoders; put() encodes whatever passed Presence::check.

e4uw (low_battery rule) and 4qlx (trailing bytes) are separate. umgp is the Python Presence.from_cbor peer, not this file.

Fix: decode one item, require position == len (already done), reject duplicate keys and tags, and apply the same size/depth caps as ConfigUpdate / _decode_single_cbor. Keep presence_cbor.json vectors decoding.

Perspectives: security, robustness.
